## Quantitative tracks {#tracks}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Compute GC fractions from real DNA, then add bars, a moving mean and an annotation band. Each track has an explicit unit, window and baseline.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#tracks-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-47, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
feature_palette <- c(CDS = "#3973CB", promoter = "#8B5EC4", rep_origin = "#E8A42D",
  primer_bind = "#168F86", misc_feature = "#A0ADBD", protein_bind = "#CC6485")

library(ggchord)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") scale_seq_position_continuous(
  coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
  labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))

data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19[c("accver", "length")]
feature_source <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
features <- feature_source[c("accver", "start", "end", "strand", "type", "anno")]
```

</details>

### Compute a track from actual DNA {#tracks-domain}
After this page’s preparation code, compute GC fraction in 100 bp
windows of bundled pUC19. The final shorter window uses its actual base count.



```{r example-48, eval=FALSE}
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
track_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19[c("accver", "length")]
starts <- seq.int(1L, track_seq$length, by = 100L)
bins <- data.frame(accver = track_seq$accver, start = starts,
  end = pmin(starts + 99L, track_seq$length))
bins$gc <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(bins)), function(i) {
  bases <- strsplit(substr(plasmid_example_pUC19$sequence, bins$start[i], bins$end[i]), "")[[1]]
  mean(bases %in% c("G", "C"))
}, numeric(1))
head(bins)
```


Each row of `bins` is an actual sequence window. Check its endpoints and `gc`, then map values to track height and colour.

#### Draw GC fractions {#tracks-draw-gc}


```{r example-49, eval=FALSE}
p_tracks <- ggchord(seq_data = track_seq) + geom_seq() + geom_seq_center_label() +
  geom_track_bar(aes(track_value = gc, track_fill = gc), data = bins,
    position = position_track("gc", width = unit(10, "mm"))) +
  scale_track_value_continuous("gc", limits = c(0, 1), unit = "GC fraction") +
  scale_track_fill_gradientn("gc", colours = c("#E9F1FE", "#65A1DC", "#224B9B")) +
  coord_circular() + doc_theme
p_tracks
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="../man/figures/tracks.png" title="Click to enlarge"><img src="../man/figures/tracks.png" alt="GC fractions computed from the bundled pUC19 DNA" width="1296" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>GC fractions computed from the bundled pUC19 DNA · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

The domain is 0–1, in fractions. Replace it with the actual unit/range of other
measurements. `position_track()` controls placement/physical width;
`scale_track_value_continuous()` controls numerical mapping.

### Share an ID deliberately {#tracks-sharing}
Same-ID layers share a numerical domain, including bar baselines, and must agree
on width/placement. Colour scales are scoped independently by track ID. Tiles
show interval categories, lines connect observations, bars encode interval values
relative to a baseline. Sharing a domain does not require sharing a spatial band.

### Inspect retention and limits {#tracks-diagnostics}
The export's `track_registry` and `track_diagnostics` record domains, physical
sizes, native offsets and clipping. Omitted/clipped rows do not mean zero values.
Focus tracks with `focus_ggchord_track()` using the same windows.

### Combine bars, a moving mean and annotation bands {#tracks-multiple}
Run the [circular example](#modes-circular) to obtain real `features` first.


```{r example-50, eval=FALSE}
line_bins <- transform(bins, pos = floor((start + end) / 2),
  gc_mean = as.numeric(stats::filter(gc, rep(1 / 3, 3), sides = 2)))
line_bins <- line_bins[is.finite(line_bins$gc_mean), c("accver", "pos", "gc_mean")]
categories <- features[c("accver", "start", "end", "type")]
p_multitrack <- ggchord(seq_data = track_seq) + geom_seq() + geom_seq_center_label() +
  geom_track_bar(aes(track_value = gc, track_fill = gc), data = bins,
    position = position_track("gc", width = unit(10, "mm"))) +
  geom_track_line(aes(track_value = gc_mean), data = line_bins,
    position = position_track("gc", width = unit(10, "mm")), colour = "#454D65") +
  scale_track_value_continuous("gc", limits = c(0, 1), unit = "GC fraction") +
  scale_track_fill_gradientn("gc", colours = c("#E9F1FE", "#65A1DC", "#224B9B")) +
  geom_track_tile(aes(track_fill = type), data = categories,
    position = position_track("features", order = 2, width = unit(2, "mm"))) +
  scale_track_fill_manual("features", values = feature_palette) + coord_circular() + doc_theme +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left")
focused_bins <- focus_ggchord_track(bins, track_seq,
  loci = data.frame(accver = track_seq$accver, start = 500, end = 1500), type = "interval")
p_multitrack
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="../man/figures/multitrack.png" title="Click to enlarge"><img src="../man/figures/multitrack.png" alt="pUC19 GC fractions, a three-bin moving mean and annotation bands" width="1296" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>pUC19 GC fractions, a three-bin moving mean and annotation bands · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Bars and line use the same actual GC measurements; the line is a three-window
moving mean. Incomplete end windows are omitted, not filled with invented values.
Line positions use integer bin midpoints. Annotation bands have an independent ID
and palette. Bands are explicitly ordered outside; overly wide inner bands at
small radii can fold and are rejected.

### Check your result {#tracks-check-result}
GC in bins lies between 0 and 1; each row is an actual window and the last may be shorter than 100 bp. Continuous colour expresses values; the category band expresses feature types, not GC magnitude.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#output">Export, preview and diagnostics →</a></div>

### Save this result {#tracks-save-result}
Save the plot just created to the working directory; use matching dimensions for preview.

```{r example-51, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("pUC19-tracks.png", p_multitrack, width = 9, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


## Primers, restriction and feature search {#recognition}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Search known DNA for primers, restriction sites and common features, then choose a display. Computational matches and experimental validation are different.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#recognition-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

```{r example-52, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
```

### Search and display are separate {#recognition-search}
Use the bundled pUC19 DNA for exact catalogue-primer and selected restriction searches:


```{r example-53, eval=FALSE}
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
target <- setNames(plasmid_example_pUC19$sequence, plasmid_example_pUC19$accver)
primers <- find_primer_bindings(target, set = "universal")
sites <- find_restriction_sites(target, enzymes = c("EcoRI", "BamHI", "HindIII"), methylation = "none")
p_sites <- ggchord(seq_data = plasmid_example_pUC19[c("accver", "length")]) + geom_seq() +
  geom_primer(data = primers, colour = "#168F86") +
  geom_restriction_site(data = sites, colour = "#29364B") + coord_circular()
p_sites
```


Search supports circular-origin binding; set `circular = FALSE` for a linear sequence.
The actual pUC19 hits shown here should be inspected in the returned table. Search hits are computational matches, not experimental validation.
Primer `"three_prime"` mode finds an exact suffix, with no mismatch model;
its Wallace melting-temperature estimate is a composition heuristic.

### Restriction interpretation {#recognition-restriction}
`find_restriction_sites()` returns unfiltered matches and cleavage coordinates;
`filter_restriction_sites()` selects a display set. Enzyme site counts refer to
the full supplied sequence and remain stable after filtering. `methylation =
"auto"` uses audited context only for exactly recognized bundled references;
it does not claim unknown samples are unblocked. This example explicitly uses `"none"`; this is a search assumption, not a measurement
of methylation in a physical sample. `geom_restriction_site(leader = "radial")` is the default route.

### General feature recognition {#recognition-features}
`find_common_features()` supports curated exact-reference annotations, DNA and
record-specific matching modes. Protein searches use standard-code six-frame
translation; they do not implement splicing, alternative initiation or
origin-crossing protein matches. Source genetic-code metadata does not select
another translation table. For nonstandard codes use DNA matching or external
code-aware analysis. Confidence is a heuristic label, not a probability.
Use [explicit CDS projection](#projection) for known protein/genome maps.

### Follow an annotated reference workflow {#recognition-reference}
This short workflow uses the same source-backed plasmid as the complete map. The [complete pUC19
workflow](#plasmids) demonstrates catalogue annotations, exact reference
matching, site display filtering, primer labels and feature stacking together.
Changing only a sequence name does not make it a recognized reference; sequence
content determines source-backed recognition. Read the result methods and
methylation provenance instead of assigning reference claims to an unknown sample.

### Check your result {#recognition-check-result}
Inspect match positions, methods and provenance. Restriction filtering is a display choice; methylation search conditions are not a measurement of an unknown sample.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#plasmids">A complete circular annotation workflow →</a></div>


## Compare CDS neighbourhoods {#homology}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Compare AmpR neighbourhoods in two plasmids. Check real coding DNA, establish correspondence, then focus to each CDS plus 200 bp on either side.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#homology-prepare}
Only bundled data is needed; no download or new alignment. Load the package and optional display settings first.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-54, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") scale_seq_position_continuous(
  coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
  labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
```

</details>

### 1. Extract actual CDS and coding DNA {#homology-membership}
Select AmpR annotations from bundled pUC19 and pETDuet-1, retaining IDs, coordinates, strand and text. Reverse-complement negative-strand DNA so comparisons use the same biological orientation rather than annotation names alone.


```{r example-55, eval=FALSE}
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
data(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_source <- rbind(plasmid_example_pUC19, plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_seq <- homolog_source[c("accver", "length")]
cluster_features <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(homolog_source)), function(i) {
  f <- find_common_features(homolog_source[i, ])
  f[f$type == "CDS" & f$anno == "AmpR", c("accver", "start", "end", "strand", "anno")]
}))
cluster_features$feature_id <- with(cluster_features, paste(accver, start, end, sep = ":"))
# Membership is computed from exact strand-corrected CDS DNA equality, not gene names.
cds_dna <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cluster_features)), function(i) {
  f <- cluster_features[i, ]; dna <- homolog_source$sequence[match(f$accver, homolog_source$accver)]
  dna <- substr(dna, f$start, f$end)
  if (f$strand == "-") dna <- chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", paste(rev(strsplit(dna, "")[[1]]), collapse = ""))
  dna
}, "")
```


`cluster_features` should contain two actual CDS; `cds_dna` retains their oriented coding sequences. This strict example checks exact DNA equality. General homology analysis can use external alignments and clustering; homologs need not be identical.

### 2. Declare members and sequence pairs {#homology-links}
Build membership from exact coding-DNA equality. Different DNA does not enter one group merely because both annotations say AmpR.


```{r example-56, eval=FALSE}
membership <- data.frame(feature_id = cluster_features$feature_id,
  cluster_id = paste0("exact_CDS_", match(cds_dna, unique(cds_dna))))
homologs <- link_ggchord_clusters(cluster_features, membership,
  pairs = data.frame(qaccver = homolog_seq$accver[1], saccver = homolog_seq$accver[2]))
loci <- find_ggchord_loci(homolog_seq, cluster_features,
  targets = cluster_features$feature_id[cluster_features$anno == "AmpR"][1], upstream = 100, downstream = 100)
```


Inspect `membership` and `homologs$report$comparisons` and `$members`. The linking utility consumes existing groups; it does not compute a new alignment. Unknown members and ambiguous paralogs are reported; only explicit `paralogs = "all"` requests all combinations within the documented bounds.

### 3. Focus on comparable neighbourhoods {#homology-focus}
Full plasmid lengths would shrink the individual CDS. Construct windows from each real CDS source interval and add 200 bp on either side, retaining the original sequence and annotation tables.


```{r example-57, eval=FALSE}
# Compare equivalent local windows instead of shrinking one gene on full plasmids.
homolog_windows <- cluster_features[c("accver", "start", "end")]
local_homologs <- focus_ggchord_data(homolog_seq, homologs$data, cluster_features,
  loci = homolog_windows, expand = 200)
p_homologs <- ggchord(seq_data = local_homologs$seq_data,
  ribbon_data = local_homologs$ribbon_data, gene_data = local_homologs$gene_data) +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#8D7AC6", alpha = .65) + geom_seq(colour = "#253954", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_feature(data = local_homologs$gene_data, feature_fill = "#D79A24",
    position = position_strand(.10), width = .07) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = local_homologs$gene_data, size = 4, label_fit = "shrink") +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) + geom_seq_break() +
  coord_collinear() + doc_axis("source") + doc_theme
p_homologs
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="../man/figures/homologs.png" title="Click to enlarge"><img src="../man/figures/homologs.png" alt="AmpR neighbourhoods: identical CDS, 200 bp flanks and source coordinates" width="1440" height="720" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>AmpR neighbourhoods: identical CDS, 200 bp flanks and source coordinates · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Gold arrows identify the checked identical coding sequences; the purple band connects their CDS ranges and internal text names AmpR. Axes use each original sequence's positions, so one horizontal location can have different source labels. Break markers indicate that only local windows remain.

`local_homologs$report` records retention and clipping. Genes outside the windows are omitted, not absent. The band represents declared interval correspondence, not a base alignment; envelopes of segmented annotations likewise do not establish exon-level correspondence.

### 4. Project supported protein intervals to both CDS {#homology-projection}

```{r example-58, eval=FALSE}
# Exact CDS DNA equality supplies evidence for these selected ungapped residues.
matching <- homologs$data[1, ]
paired_coding <- transform(cluster_features, phase = 0)
paired_cds <- build_ggchord_cds(paired_coding)
protein_link <- data.frame(qfeature_id = matching$qfeature_id, sfeature_id = matching$sfeature_id,
  qstart = 1, qend = 20, sstart = 1, send = 20)
projected_links <- project_ggchord_links(protein_link, paired_cds, ungapped = TRUE)
projected_links
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Projected genomic feature rows | 1 |
| Projected nucleotide link rows | 1 |

The first 20 residues of identical CDS provide sequence evidence for `ungapped = TRUE`. Equal spans alone do not justify that claim for ordinary BLASTp HSPs. The utility retains protein statistics rather than presenting them as nucleotide identity.

### Check your result {#homology-check-result}
Both internal labels should read AmpR and arrows retain the actual negative strand. Coding DNA supports correspondence; source axes and focus reports explain the local display. Save at [explicit 10 × 5 in dimensions](#output).

Next: [read real BLASTp query intervals](#alignments-protein), understand [CDS projection and segments](#projection), or create [independent local windows](#views).

### Save this result {#homology-save-result}
Save the plot just created to the working directory; use matching dimensions for preview.

```{r example-59, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("ampR-neighbourhood.png", p_homologs, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


## Project protein intervals to genomic coordinates {#projection}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Project known protein intervals to genomic positions through real CDS, retaining phase, strand and segmentation explicitly.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#projection-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-60, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") scale_seq_position_continuous(
  coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
  labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))

data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
data(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_source <- rbind(plasmid_example_pUC19, plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_seq <- homolog_source[c("accver", "length")]
cluster_features <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(homolog_source)), function(i) {
  f <- find_common_features(homolog_source[i, ])
  f[f$type == "CDS" & f$anno == "AmpR", c("accver", "start", "end", "strand", "anno")]
}))
cluster_features$feature_id <- with(cluster_features, paste(accver, start, end, sep = ":"))
# Membership is computed from exact strand-corrected CDS DNA equality, not gene names.
cds_dna <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cluster_features)), function(i) {
  f <- cluster_features[i, ]; dna <- homolog_source$sequence[match(f$accver, homolog_source$accver)]
  dna <- substr(dna, f$start, f$end)
  if (f$strand == "-") dna <- chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", paste(rev(strsplit(dna, "")[[1]]), collapse = ""))
  dna
}, "")

membership <- data.frame(feature_id = cluster_features$feature_id,
  cluster_id = paste0("exact_CDS_", match(cds_dna, unique(cds_dna))))
homologs <- link_ggchord_clusters(cluster_features, membership,
  pairs = data.frame(qaccver = homolog_seq$accver[1], saccver = homolog_seq$accver[2]))
loci <- find_ggchord_loci(homolog_seq, cluster_features,
  targets = cluster_features$feature_id[cluster_features$anno == "AmpR"][1], upstream = 100, downstream = 100)

# Compare equivalent local windows instead of shrinking one gene on full plasmids.
homolog_windows <- cluster_features[c("accver", "start", "end")]
local_homologs <- focus_ggchord_data(homolog_seq, homologs$data, cluster_features,
  loci = homolog_windows, expand = 200)
p_homologs <- ggchord(seq_data = local_homologs$seq_data,
  ribbon_data = local_homologs$ribbon_data, gene_data = local_homologs$gene_data) +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#8D7AC6", alpha = .65) + geom_seq(colour = "#253954", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_feature(data = local_homologs$gene_data, feature_fill = "#D79A24",
    position = position_strand(.10), width = .07) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = local_homologs$gene_data, size = 4, label_fit = "shrink") +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) + geom_seq_break() +
  coord_collinear() + doc_axis("source") + doc_theme
p_homologs
```

</details>

### Start with source-backed CDS {#projection-cds}
Run the [identical-CDS comparison](#homology-membership) first. It uses real
bundled plasmid annotations and DNA. Complete CDS use explicit phase 0 and
translation table 11.


```{r example-61, eval=FALSE}
# Run the exact-CDS comparison first; these are complete source-backed CDS.
coding <- transform(cluster_features, phase = 0)
cds <- build_ggchord_cds(coding, genetic_code = 11)
# This selects residues for a display example; it does not claim a detected domain.
domains <- data.frame(feature_id = "selected_residues", parent_id = coding$feature_id[1], start = 2, end = 20)
genomic <- project_ggchord_features(domains, cds)
genomic
```


This example selects residues 2–20 for display; it does not claim a detected
protein domain. Projection returns genomic intervals with strand/segment context.
Actual domains require exact parent CDS IDs and amino-acid ranges; annotation
names or maximum feature endpoints cannot supply missing evidence.

### Segments, phase and partial regions {#projection-boundaries}
`build_ggchord_cds()` constructs a segment map; `project_ggchord_features()` then
splits amino-acid intervals through it. Crossing a boundary can return several
rows; multiplying coordinates by three is insufficient. Inspect policies/reports
for partial CDS, phase and truncation. DNA matching, interval projection and
actual translation/alignment are distinct operations.

### BLASTp query spans and two-ended links {#projection-links}

```{r example-62, eval=FALSE}
# Exact CDS DNA equality supplies evidence for these selected ungapped residues.
matching <- homologs$data[1, ]
paired_coding <- transform(cluster_features, phase = 0)
paired_cds <- build_ggchord_cds(paired_coding)
protein_link <- data.frame(qfeature_id = matching$qfeature_id, sfeature_id = matching$sfeature_id,
  qstart = 1, qend = 20, sstart = 1, send = 20)
projected_links <- project_ggchord_links(protein_link, paired_cds, ungapped = TRUE)
projected_links
```


This ungapped case relies on [verified identical coding DNA](#homology).
Real BLASTp HSPs may contain gaps: query spans can still be projected, but paired
links need the subject CDS and justified ungapped correspondence. See
[real BLASTp import/projection](#alignments-protein). This version does not
reinterpret aa as bp or add native protein-coordinate plotting.

### Check your result {#projection-check-result}
Check parent CDS IDs, projection reports and returned segments. The selected residue range is a display example, not a detected domain.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#alignments">Import nucleotide and protein alignments →</a></div>


## Focus, segments and homology {#views}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Select local windows or segments while keeping source positions distinct from display transformations.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#views-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-63, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example[c("accver", "length")]
links <- ribbon_data_example[c("qaccver", "saccver", "qstart", "qend", "sstart", "send")]
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- transform(gene_data_example, strand = source_strand)[c("accver", "start", "end", "strand")]

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(c("#3867D6", "#E58A28", "#219B83", "#9B59B6"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1"))
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#3B6FD8", "-" = "#E1812C", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") scale_seq_position_continuous(
  coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
  labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
```

</details>

### Focus without losing origins {#views-focus}
After this page’s preparation code:


```{r example-64, eval=FALSE}
focus_loci <- data.frame(accver = seqs$accver,
  start = floor(seqs$length * .25), end = floor(seqs$length * .75))
focused <- focus_ggchord_data(seqs, links, genes, loci = focus_loci)
p_focus <- ggchord(seq_data = focused$seq_data, ribbon_data = focused$ribbon_data,
  gene_data = focused$gene_data) + geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#7199DF", alpha = .5) + geom_gene() + geom_seq_break() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) + scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  doc_axis("source") + coord_collinear() + doc_theme
p_focus
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="../man/figures/focus.png" title="Click to enlarge"><img src="../man/figures/focus.png" alt="Focused sequence windows with source-coordinate axes" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Focused sequence windows with source-coordinate axes · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Focus relocates retained positions to local one-based coordinates and retains
source origins, truncation flags and a report. `boundary = "trim"` can clip
links by a linear display projection; it does not realign sequences. A scaled
alignment length is flagged as estimated. `coordinates = "source"` restores
source axis labels, including after repeated focusing.

### Independent windows and local reversal {#views-segments}

```{r example-65, eval=FALSE}
windows <- data.frame(accver = rep(seqs$accver[1], 2),
  start = c(1, floor(seqs$length[1] * .65)), end = c(floor(seqs$length[1] * .4), seqs$length[1]),
  locus_id = c("left_window", "right_window"), row_id = seqs$accver[1], orientation = c(1, -1))
segmented <- segment_ggchord_data(seqs[1, ], windows = windows)
p_segments <- ggchord(seq_data = segmented$seq_data) + geom_seq() +
  coord_collinear(segments = segmented$segments, segment_gap = 2000)
p_segments
```


Each window has a reversible source mapping; omitted gaps have no mapping.
`map_ggchord_position()` maps explicit source positions into a plot for ordinary
ggplot2 annotations. Supply the window ID when windows share a source sequence.
Do not interpret display orientation as a change to the original strand.

### Explicit biological relationships {#views-homology}
`find_ggchord_loci()` selects declared feature/name queries. `link_ggchord_clusters()`
requires an explicit membership table and sequence pairs; equal gene names do
not establish homology. `filter_ggchord_ribbons()`, `deduplicate_ggchord_ribbons()`
and `merge_ggchord_ribbons()` prepare existing alignments, preserving source
membership and estimated-length flags. Bundle and density statistics summarize
provided links rather than creating new sequence alignments.

### Map an annotation back to source coordinates {#views-mapping}

```{r example-66, eval=FALSE}
source_position <- focus_loci$start[1] + 100
source_mark <- map_ggchord_position(p_focus, seqs$accver[1], source_position, source = TRUE)
p_marked <- p_focus + ggplot2::geom_point(data = source_mark, aes(x, y),
  inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#9B59B6", size = 3)
p_marked
```


Run the [focus example](#views-focus) first. The helper returns Cartesian x/y
for a source position 100 bp inside the first selected window. It does not make all ordinary ggplot2 coordinates
become genomic bp. In segmented views choose the window ID, and check positions
in omitted gaps rather than extrapolating across them. Use [explicit homologs](#homology)
when the locus selection comes from declared feature/cluster evidence.

### Check your result {#views-check-result}
Inspect cropping reports, break markers and source coordinates. Omitted gaps have no mapping; a display flip alone is not evidence of inversion.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#homology">Explicit homologs and coding-coordinate links →</a></div>


## Mappings, scales, guides and themes {#styling}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Give colours a clear meaning: identify categories or continuous quantities, then choose mappings, scales and guides. Website accents do not dictate data colours.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#styling-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-67, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example[c("accver", "length")]
links <- ribbon_data_example[c("qaccver", "saccver", "qstart", "qend", "sstart", "send")]
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- transform(gene_data_example, strand = source_strand)[c("accver", "start", "end", "strand")]

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(c("#3867D6", "#E58A28", "#219B83", "#9B59B6"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1"))
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#3B6FD8", "-" = "#E1812C", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") scale_seq_position_continuous(
  coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
  labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
```

</details>

### Build styles from data roles {#styling-roles}
Run this page’s preparation code below. The example declares categories
explicitly: ribbon fill maps query ID; sequence colour maps sequence ID; gene fill
maps strand. Manual scale names match those values exactly.


```{r example-68, eval=FALSE}
p_styled <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = links, gene_data = genes) + geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = qaccver), alpha = .5) + geom_gene() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) + coord_collinear() + doc_axis() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) + scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  guides(gene_fill = guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1)) + doc_theme
theme_variants <- list(minimal = theme_ggchord_minimal(), dark = theme_ggchord_dark(), plasmid = theme_ggchord_plasmid())
p_styled
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="../man/figures/styling.png" title="Click to enlarge"><img src="../man/figures/styling.png" alt="Explicit sequence, strand and query-category colour scales" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Explicit sequence, strand and query-category colour scales · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

| Role | Mapped data | Useful scale family |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seq_colour`, `seq_ring` | Sequence/category | Sequence colour or ring manual scales |
| `ribbon_fill`, `ribbon_alpha`, `ribbon_colour`, `ribbon_linetype` | Alignment metadata or statistics | Manual, gradient/steps/identity and alpha scales |
| `feature_fill`, `feature_shape`, `gene_fill`, `region_fill` | Annotation category or strand | Role-specific manual/preset scales |
| `link_colour`, `link_alpha`, `link_linewidth`, `link_linetype` | Point-link metadata | Continuous or manual link scales |
| `track_value`, `track_fill`, `track_colour` | Values/categories in one named track | Named value domain and colour/fill scales |

### Fixed styles and user scale priority {#styling-priority}
Put a constant style outside `aes()`. Map variable styles inside it and supply an
appropriate scale. An explicitly fixed geom value takes precedence; omitting that
argument keeps mapping active. Your scale takes priority over automatic defaults.
Repeated same-kind layers keep independent data/mapping/parameters. A geometric
vector named by `accver` does not mean a scale also accepts per-sequence lists.

### Make legends readable {#styling-guides}
`guide_ggchord_legend()` controls discrete role legends; `guide_ggchord_colourbar()`
controls continuous colour guides. The colour/color spelling aliases are retained,
with `colour` preferred in this documentation. Use `show.legend` on a layer,
`guides()` for guide choices and `theme(legend.position = ...)` for placement.
A wide guide may need multiple rows or a wider export, not smaller biological data.

### Select a theme for the scene {#styling-themes}
The example stores minimal, dark and plasmid alternatives in `theme_variants`.
Add the appropriate object to the matching plot. `theme_ggchord_publication()`
is used above; the plasmid preset belongs with the circular workflow. These
objects style non-data appearance. They do not choose a coordinate system or
replace data-driven fill scales. Use `theme(text = element_text(...))` for text
appearance; removed `base_size` constructor-style shortcuts have a
[migration route](#migration).

### Check your result {#styling-check-result}
Links from the same query share a colour; continuous identity needs a continuous scale. Put fixed colours outside aes() and make each guide explain its mapping.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#adjustments">Common adjustments and grammar →</a></div>


## Common adjustments and grammar {#adjustments}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Put common adjustments in the appropriate ggplot2 component: mappings, geometry, positions, coordinates and themes have distinct roles.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#adjustments-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-69, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example[c("accver", "length")]
links <- ribbon_data_example[c("qaccver", "saccver", "qstart", "qend", "sstart", "send")]
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- transform(gene_data_example, strand = source_strand)[c("accver", "start", "end", "strand")]

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(c("#3867D6", "#E58A28", "#219B83", "#9B59B6"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1"))
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#3B6FD8", "-" = "#E1812C", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") scale_seq_position_continuous(
  coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
  labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
```

</details>

### Assign each responsibility {#adjustments-grammar}
| Task | Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Map a column to an aesthetic | `aes()` |
| Define mapping and guide | `scale_*()`, `guides()` |
| Geometry and fixed style | `geom_*()` |
| Local placement | `position_*()` |
| Global coordinate system | `coord_*()` |
| Non-data appearance | `theme_*()`, `theme()` |
| Titles and captions | `labs()` |

Fixed styles may be supplied directly to geoms. Data-driven variation needs a
mapping and scale. An explicit fixed value overrides its mapping; omitting the
fixed argument preserves the mapping. User scales override inferred defaults.
`shape` is the fixed feature geometry parameter; `feature_shape` remains the
mapped role. Explicit `shape = NULL` is invalid, not a request to use a mapping.

### Map link identity {#adjustments-mapping}
After this page’s preparation code:


```{r example-70, eval=FALSE}
identity_links <- ribbon_data_example[c("qaccver", "saccver", "qstart", "qend", "sstart", "send", "pident")]
p_mapped <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = identity_links) + geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = pident), alpha = .6) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#3D2185", "#C74678", "#F6B739"), name = "Identity (%)") +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  coord_chord(rotation = 20) + labs(title = "Sequence comparison") + doc_theme
p_mapped
```


### Place features {#adjustments-position}
Use `position_strand(c("+" = .1, "-" = -.2))` for signed strand offsets.
`position_feature_stack()` handles overlapping features; `position_track()`
allocates a named quantitative lane. Geometric sequence parameters accept one
value, a matching unnamed vector, or a vector named by `accver`; named vectors
are recommended. This syntax does not extend to scales, guides or themes.

Each layer owns its own `data`, `mapping` and parameters. Repeated feature or
link layers do not replace one another. Use ordinary ggplot2 `show.legend` and
`inherit.aes`; role input mappings precede geometry, while staged visual mappings
follow ggplot2 evaluation. See the API contract (`help("ggchord_api_contract", package = "ggchord")`).

### Check your result {#adjustments-check-result}
Use a coordinate for global rotation, named values for per-sequence geometry, and mappings plus scales for data-dependent colour.

## Export, preview and diagnostics {#output}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Inspect figures at their actual export dimensions, save with standard ggsave(), and understand what layout tables and diagnostics establish.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#output-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-71, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example[c("accver", "length")]
links <- ribbon_data_example[c("qaccver", "saccver", "qstart", "qend", "sstart", "send")]
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- transform(gene_data_example, strand = source_strand)[c("accver", "start", "end", "strand")]

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(c("#3867D6", "#E58A28", "#219B83", "#9B59B6"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1"))
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#3B6FD8", "-" = "#E1812C", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") scale_seq_position_continuous(
  coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
  labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))

anchor_rows <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(genes)), genes$accver), function(i)
  i[which.max(genes$end[i] - genes$start[i])]))
anchors <- genes[anchor_rows, c("accver", "start", "end")]
p_collinear <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = links, gene_data = genes) +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = qaccver), alpha = .7) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_manual(values = seq_palette, guide = "none") + geom_seq() +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(.1)) + geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  coord_collinear(anchor = anchors, align = "center", orientation = "auto") + doc_axis() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) + doc_theme
p_collinear
```

</details>

### Save the intended size {#output-size}
After creating `p_collinear` in [three modes](#modes):


```{r example-72, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("comparison.png", p_collinear, width = 8, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


RStudio's Plots pane uses the current panel size and can rearrange labels and
guides. Preview at the same explicit dimensions before final `ggsave()`:


```{r example-73, eval=FALSE}
view_ggchord(p_collinear, width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
diagnosis <- diagnose_ggchord(p_collinear, width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
```


`view_ggchord()` returns a temporary image path; it does not keep a final export.
The website, README and vignettes share PNG assets exported through standard
`ggsave()` at sizes listed in the [gallery](#gallery). They do not capture an
interactively resized panel. Use your intended PDF/SVG device explicitly for
final vector output; font availability and embedding remain device-dependent.

### Consume geometry by name {#output-geometry}

```{r example-74, eval=FALSE}
geometry <- export_ggchord_layout(p_collinear, include = "seq")
rows <- unique(geometry$seq[c("layer_id", "component", "source_row")])
```


`export_ggchord_layout()` is the recommended layer-aware table interface.
`get_chord_layout()` retains the complete documented layout; neither is deprecated.
Select named fields, not fixed column positions. `source_row` indexes resolved
layer input; IDs are build-local resources, not permanent biological identifiers.
See the complete layout contract (`help("ggchord_layout_contract", package = "ggchord")`).

### Interpret evidence {#output-diagnostics}
`diagnose_ggchord()` separates measured panel size from geometry convergence.
A measured panel does not certify collision-free text, font embedding or all
applications. Inspect warnings, text/guide measurements and placement reasons.
`optimize_ggchord_layout()` applies documented opt-in adjustments; retain a copy
and inspect the result. Previews and diagnostics use independent render copies.
Direct mutation of shared ggproto layer environments retains ordinary ggplot2
reference semantics; it is not an automatically isolated edit.

### Complete layout, tables and opt-in ordering {#output-consumption}

```{r example-75, eval=FALSE}
full_layout <- get_chord_layout(p_collinear)
layer_tables <- export_ggchord_layout(p_collinear, include = c("seq", "gene"), original_data = TRUE)
layout_choice <- optimize_ggchord_layout(seqs, links, optimize = c("order", "orientation"), weight = "count")
```


Create `p_collinear` in [three modes](#modes-collinear) first.
`full_layout` retains the complete documented getter result. `layer_tables`
selects sequence/gene tables and resolved original data; it is not a raw-file
archive. Layer IDs and source-row roles distinguish independent same-kind layers.
Empty components can lack a fixed column prototype. Select fields by name.

`layout_choice` optimizes declared order/orientation using count weighting because
the minimal plotting table deliberately omits alignment-length statistics. It returns a choice
for explicit use in sequence settings; it does not mutate the plot or establish
biological orientation. Save the choice and compare the result before adopting it.
The export asset manifest (`website/assets/plots.csv` in the source repository) records exact documentation sizes.

### Check your result {#output-check-result}
Use matching dimensions for preview and saving. Inspect text, guides and warnings; a successful measurement does not certify fonts or release quality across devices.

## Frequently asked questions {#faq}

### Why are labels different after resizing? {#faq-resize}
The available physical space changed. Use [explicit-size preview and saving](#output-size).
Check hidden-label diagnostics; do not infer missing input rows from absent text.

### Why did an old parameter stop working? {#faq-removed}
The API cleanup removed execution of old aliases. Use the [migration table](#migration).
Do not mix old and new spellings for one semantic setting. The colour/color
function spelling aliases remain, with `colour` preferred in documentation.

### Why is a feature rejected as a gene? {#faq-strand}
The gene shortcut requires known `+`/`-` strand. Keep unknown strand in a general
feature layer; do not guess `+`. Amino-acid intervals require explicit projection.

### Why is a ribbon missing in linear mode? {#faq-ribbons}
By default ribbons connect adjacent displayed sequences. Inspect pair selection,
clipping and validation. Use explicit `pairs` or `adjacent_only = FALSE` deliberately.
This default does not remove original input records.

### Can the package compute alignments or validate primer experiments? {#faq-biology}
It visualizes supplied alignments and computational search results. It does not
run BLAST, infer clusters from names or validate wet-lab outcomes. Search confidence
is not a probability. See [recognition limitations](#recognition).

### Is a measured diagnostic a release certification? {#faq-quality}
No. It describes a requested render. Platform/device/font checks, full vignettes
and package checks belong to an explicitly authorized release. This development
version has only scoped documentation verification.

### Where should I report a problem? {#faq-report}
Use the [issue tracker](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/issues) with a small input,
package/ggplot2 versions, code, intended width/height, device and diagnostic output.
Avoid attaching private sequence data; a synthetic reproduction is usually enough.


## Migrate to the candidate API {#migration}

### Scope and timing {#migration-scope}
These are current candidate replacements, not a v1.0.0 compatibility promise.
Earlier 0.16.x versions are locally completed but unreleased. Old calls in this
table explain migration and must not be executed as current examples. Exact
first-removal tags are not guessed where historical evidence gives only an upper bound.

### Replacement table {#migration-table}
| Old (do not run) | Current | Removal / guard | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `geom_ribbon()` | `geom_link_ribbon()` | ≤ 0.16.1 | Renamed link layer; not ggplot2::geom_ribbon(). |
| `ggchord(..., rotation = 20)` | `ggchord(...) + coord_chord(rotation = 20)` | ≤ 0.16.1 | Global coordinates are composed with +. |
| `geom_feature(feature_shape = "block", feature_width = .05)` | `geom_feature(shape = "block", width = .05)` | 0.16.1 | Mapped feature_shape is retained. |
| `geom_gene(gene_offset = c("+" = .1, "-" = .2))` | `geom_gene(position = position_strand(c("+" = .1, "-" = -.2)))` | 0.16.1 | Explicit Position values are signed. |
| `geom_feature(feature_offset = .1)` | `geom_feature(position = position_strand(.1))` | 0.16.1 | Use a Position object. |
| `geom_gene(gene_width = .05)` | `geom_gene(width = .05)` | 0.16.1 | Fixed geometry uses the shared width name. |
| `geom_link_ribbon(ribbon_gap = .01)` | `geom_link_ribbon(link_gap = .01)` | 0.16.1 | Use link_gap; likewise use link_ctrl_point. |
| `geom_gene_label_repel(gene_label_layout = "aligned")` | `geom_gene_label_repel(label_layout = "auto")` | 0.16.1 | Migrate both the name and value. |
| `geom_gene_label_repel(label_rotation = 90)` | `geom_gene_label(label_rotation = 90)` | 0.16.4 guard | Previously ignored manual control now errors; alternatively remove it. |
| `geom_feature_label_repel(label_orientation = "horizontal")` | `geom_feature_label(label_orientation = "horizontal")` | 0.16.4 guard | Use the fixed feature-label layer for unknown-strand features. |
| `geom_restriction_site(leader = "trunk")` | `geom_restriction_site(leader = "radial")` | 0.16.1 | The radial default remains. |
| `theme_ggchord(base_size = 10)` | `theme_ggchord() + theme(text = element_text(size = 10))` | ≤ 0.16.1 | Text appearance belongs to theme elements. |

### Run the replacement {#migration-replacement}
In a fresh session, run this preparation before the current replacements:

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-76, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example[c("accver", "length")]
links <- ribbon_data_example[c("qaccver", "saccver", "qstart", "qend", "sstart", "send")]
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- transform(gene_data_example, strand = source_strand)[c("accver", "start", "end", "strand")]

data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19[c("accver", "length")]
feature_source <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
features <- feature_source[c("accver", "start", "end", "strand", "type", "anno")]
```

</details>


```{r example-77, eval=FALSE}
p_migrated <- ggchord(plasmid_seq) + geom_seq() +
  geom_feature(data = features, shape = "block", width = .05) +
  geom_feature_label(data = features, label_rotation = 0) + coord_circular()
p_offsets <- ggchord(seqs, gene_data = genes) + geom_seq() +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(c("+" = .1, "-" = -.2)))
```


Old minus-strand offset magnitudes need a negative sign in explicit Position
values. Mapping still uses `aes(feature_shape = type)` with a shape scale;
the fixed parameter is `shape`. Automatic labels use `label_layout`; manual
geometry uses the corresponding fixed-label layer. `label_layout = "aligned"`
becomes `"auto"`. Removed names are errors, not silently retained execution paths.

### What remains supported {#migration-retained}
The five colour/color spelling aliases, all upstream reexports, gene/feature/plasmid
shortcuts and both geometry getter/export interfaces remain. Coordinate-specific
defaults and already documented result fields are retained. See the
API contract (`help("ggchord_api_contract", package = "ggchord")`) and current reference for
NULL/NA/missing semantics; NULL does not universally mean disabled.

### One source for both languages {#gallery-source}
All figures use bundled source-backed data or attributed real input records, defined in the shared
[documentation example source](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/blob/main/tools/documentation-examples.R).
No raw FASTA/GFF3/BLAST record was changed to improve appearance. The same image
bytes are used by both languages, README and vignette; captions provide localized
interpretation. The source and asset hashes are recorded in the asset manifest (`website/assets/plots.csv` in the source repository).

Display filters are stated in the relevant articles. GC is computed from actual
DNA; exact-CDS membership is checked from sequence content. Deliberate corruption
is confined to diagnostic examples and is never presented as biological data.

### Reproduce {#gallery-reproduce}
From the source repository, with its suggested development dependencies available:

```sh
Rscript tools/documentation-plots.R
python3 tools/sync-tutorials.py --check
python3 tools/build-website.py
python3 tools/check-documentation.py
```

The PNG device is used only to update these documentation figures. This is not
an output-device matrix or release validation. Source code and dimensions live
in `tools/documentation-plots.R`; changing the figure parameters requires
regenerating the manifest. See [output](#output) for your own export.

### Asset sources {#gallery-assets}
[Artwork, template and dependency licenses](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/blob/main/website/ASSET-SOURCES.md).


## Terminology and design sources {#glossary}

### Shared terminology {#glossary-terms}
| English | 现代汉语 | API / units |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sequence | 序列 | accver / length |
| chord diagram | 弦图 | coord_chord() |
| circular sequence map | 单序列圆图 | coord_circular() |
| collinearity plot | 共线性图 | coord_collinear() |
| interval link / ribbon | 区间连接 / 连接带 | qaccver / saccver |
| feature | 通用注释特征（feature） | geom_feature() |
| gene | 已知链的基因 | geom_gene() |
| strand | 链方向 | + / - / unknown |
| aesthetic mapping | 美学属性映射 | aes() |
| scale | 标度 | scale_*() |
| guide | 图例 / 标度指南 | guides() |
| position | 局部位置调整 | position_*() |
| track | 定量轨道 | position_track() |
| genomic position | 基因组位置 | one-based inclusive bp / 一基闭区间 |
| layout units | 原生布局单位 | not bp or mm / 不等于 bp 或 mm |
| source row | 已解析输入来源行 | source_row |
| physical file line | 物理文件行 | .source_line |
| focus | 局部聚焦 | focus_ggchord_data() |
| segment | 分段窗口 | segment_ggchord_data() |
| leader | 标签引导线 | label / connection |
| CDS projection | 编码序列坐标投影 | build_ggchord_cds() |
| measured panel | 已测量面板 | not visual certification / 不等于视觉认证 |

### Design and asset provenance {#glossary-sources}
The grammar follows [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/): mappings, scales,
geometry, positions, coordinates and themes retain distinct responsibilities.
Compact query/subject field names follow BLAST-style tables; ggchord does not run
an alignment tool during drawing. Circular hierarchy and feature readability
are compared with Circos, clinker and DNA Features Viewer, as recorded in the
repository design documents. These are conceptual comparisons, not copied APIs.

The detailed ggchord artwork was supplied by the user on 2026-11-01 for this
website and documentation. Full-size PNG and WebP preserve every decoded RGBA
pixel. Only the small navigation thumbnail is resized. See the image manifest (`website/assets/icon.json` in the source repository)
for source hashes and exact sizes. The compact hexagonal study mark below, site
CSS/JS and documentation diagrams are original project assets under the
repository MIT terms. The study mark is supplementary, not a replacement for
the supplied artwork.

![Compact hexagonal study mark](../man/figures/logo.svg) System fonts are used; no webfont, icon
library or third-party image is downloaded. Plot colours come from the package's
existing defaults or explicit teaching code; those literal colour choices are
listed with the source. The site uses the existing Pandoc and R documentation
converters at build time without bundling their binaries or stylesheets.
